records.sourceHebrew:
כָּךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: בָּנַי, בָּרָאתִי יֵצֶר הָרָע וּבָרָאתִי לוֹ תּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין. וְאִם אַתֶּם עוֹסְקִים בַּתּוֹרָה – אֵין אַתֶּם נִמְסָרִים בְּיָדוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הֲלוֹא אִם תֵּיטִיב שְׂאֵת״,

וְאִם אֵין אַתֶּם עוֹסְקִין בַּתּוֹרָה – אַתֶּם נִמְסָרִים בְּיָדוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לַפֶּתַח חַטָּאת רֹבֵץ״, וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁכׇּל מַשָּׂאוֹ וּמַתָּנוֹ בְּךָ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאֵלֶיךָ תְּשׁוּקָתוֹ״. וְאִם אַתָּה רוֹצֶה אַתָּה מוֹשֵׁל בּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה תִּמְשׇׁל בּוֹ״.
records.sourceEnglish: Thus the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: “My children, I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as a seasoning for it. If you occupy yourselves with Torah, you will not be handed over to its power, as it is said: ‘If you do well, shall you not be lifted up?’ But if you do not occupy yourselves with Torah, you are handed over to its power, as it is said: ‘Sin crouches at the door.’ Moreover, all its dealings are directed at you, as it is said: ‘Its desire is toward you.’ Yet if you wish, you can rule over it, as it is said: ‘And you shall rule over it.’”
records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayigash 4
records.targetHebrew: כִּי דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה הֵם עֵצָה לָאָדָם לְהִנָּצֵל מֵחֶמְדָּה, אַף בְּעִידָּנָא דְּיֵצֶר הָרַע דְּלֵית מַאן דְּמִדְּכִיר לְיֵצֶר טוֹב (נְדָרִים לָמֶד בֵּית עַמּוּד בֵּית), עַל זֶה בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָאָדָם הַמְּשׁוּקָּע בְּחֵשֶׁק וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְהִנָּצֵל מִמֶּנּוּ, אָז אֵין לוֹ עֵצָה שֶׁיִּזְכּוֹר כִּי הוּא דָּבָר אָסוּר, כִּי אֵין כֹּחַ בְּהָאִיסּוּר כָּל כָּךְ לְהַפְרִישׁ אֶת הָאָדָם מֵרָע בְּעִידָּנָא דְּיֵצֶר הָרַע, אַךְ אָז הָעֵצָה הַיְּעוּצָה לָאָדָם שֶׁיִּזְכּוֹר, כִּי יוּכַל לִמְצֹא זֶה הַטּוֹבָה עַצְמָהּ בְּדִבְרֵי תּוֹרָה וְרַק שֶׁיְּהֵא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
records.targetEnglish: For words of Torah provide a person with a way to be rescued from craving—even when the evil inclination holds sway and no one calls the good inclination to mind (Nedarim 32b). For this, the Holy One, blessed be He, created Torah as a seasoning. In truth, when a person is immersed in desire and cannot extricate himself, merely recalling that the thing is forbidden offers him no effective counsel, since at the moment when the evil inclination holds sway, the prohibition does not have enough power to separate him from evil. At that point, the counsel for the person is to remember that he can find this very good in words of Torah, but in holiness.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach explains the Gemara’s seasoning metaphor by distinguishing a warning against the desired act from finding the good one seeks within Torah in holiness. This gives content to the claim that Torah changes the power of desire. The excerpt belongs to the Torah stage of a four-stage examination; the discourse continues with Shema and remembrance of death, so this is not a claim that an unexamined desire is already holy.

records.sourceEnglish: Thus the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: “My children, I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as a seasoning for it. If you occupy yourselves with Torah, you will not be handed over to its power, as it is said: ‘If you do well, shall you not be lifted up?’ But if you do not occupy yourselves with Torah, you are handed over to its power, as it is said: ‘Sin crouches at the door.’ Moreover, all its dealings are directed at you, as it is said: ‘Its desire is toward you.’ Yet if you wish, you can rule over it, as it is said: ‘And you shall rule over it.’”
records.targetHebrew: כְּטַעַם: "אִם פָּגַע בְּךָ וְכוּלֵי מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ" (סֻכָּה נב:), הַיְינוּ לֹא שֶׁתִּדְחֵהוּ, רַק תִּמְשְׁכֵהוּ לְשָׁם. כִּי הַתּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין כְּמוֹ דָּבָר הַמְּתַבֵּל וְעוֹשֶׂה הַבָּאוּשׁ טוֹב וְטַעַם לִשְׁבָח.
records.targetEnglish: This is the meaning of: “If [this vile one] encounters you … draw it to the house of study” (Sukkah 52b): you are not to push it away, but to draw it there. For Torah is a seasoning, like something that seasons and makes what was foul good, giving it a praiseworthy taste.
records.explanation: Rav Tzadok takes the Gemara’s word “seasoning” seriously: Torah can transform the quality of the inclination, as seasoning changes something foul into something good. He connects this to drawing the inclination into the house of study. That supplies a precise meaning for Torah’s work upon desire, rather than treating the Gemara merely as a general exhortation to study.

records.sourceHebrew: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: בְּנִי אִם פָּגַע בְּךָ מְנֻוּוֹל זֶה – מׇשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ. אִם אֶבֶן הוּא – נִימּוֹחַ, וְאִם בַּרְזֶל הוּא – מִתְפּוֹצֵץ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ נְאֻם ה׳ וּכְפַטִּישׁ יְפֹצֵץ סָלַע״. אִם אֶבֶן הוּא – נִימּוֹחַ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הוֹי כׇּל צָמֵא לְכוּ לַמַּיִם״ וְאוֹמֵר: ״אֲבָנִים שָׁחֲקוּ מַיִם״.
records.sourceEnglish: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: “My son, if this vile one encounters you, draw it to the house of study. If it is stone, it will dissolve; if it is iron, it will shatter, as it is said: ‘Are not My words like fire, declares the Lord, and like a hammer that shatters rock?’ If it is stone, it will dissolve, as it is said: ‘Ho, everyone who thirsts, go to water,’ and it also says: ‘Water wears away stones.’”

records.explanation: The instruction to “draw it” is the wording Rav Tzadok interprets in this passage, where he cites the teaching from Sukkah 52b. He reads the verb as bringing the inclination into Torah so that it is transformed, and links that reading to Torah as seasoning. The quoted paragraph therefore explains the action prescribed by this baraita, including why the encounter with Torah can change what opposed it.
